sentences.text: Primobucco is an extinct genus of birds classified in its own family, Primobucconidae, within the larger parent group Coracii.
The genus was first described in 1970 by American paleo-ornithologist Pierce Brodkorb based on a fossil right wing.
Further fossils discovered in 2010 suggest that Primobucco was an early type of roller rather than an early puffbird.
Seeds found in the digestive tracts of two specimens suggest that Primobucco was more omnivorous than modern rollers, which are exclusively predatory.
The type species, Primobucco mcgrewi, lived in North America during the Lower Eocene, spanning the Ypresian to Lutetian stages between 56 and 41.03 million years ago.
